clue.text: Give up, utterly without energy

indicators.note: 'without' tells you to drop the letter for energy from the word before it

blocks.note: quite can mean utterly, as in 'quite impossible'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone so utterly exhausted that they throw in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take QUITE and remove its E to leave QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to abandon or stop trying, a plain synonym of give up.

clue.text: Prior to unit getting broken on line

indicators.note: something broken has had its parts knocked out of order, so the word unit is rearranged
in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it in the column

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An army unit falling apart before it reaches the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time of, so it serves as a preposition equivalent to before or prior to.

clue.text: Mint upset with this metalworker

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so the letters land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint is annoyed with some craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is a craftsman who makes and repairs articles of tin or tinplate, one kind of metalworker.

clue.text: Topless omnibus, dreadful in rain cloud

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so topless means lose the opening letter
something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: omnibus with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: An open-top bus is miserable to ride in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless omnibus' paints an open-top tour bus, but topless strips the O, and dreadful shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbus is the meteorological term for a dark grey cloud bringing rain or snow.

clue.text: Shocked initially and greatly horrified at such treatment

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each following word

blocks.clueFragment: and greatly horrified at such treatment
blocks.note: the first letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone appalled by how they have been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or amazement, a close synonym of shocked.

clue.text: Mum's abandoned biggest dress

indicators.note: to have abandoned something is to have left it behind, so one word walks out of another

blocks.note: maximum means the largest or biggest
the word mum itself, the 's standing for 'has'

explanation.surface: Mother has given up on the largest frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mum's abandoned' as 'MUM has left': take MUM off the end of MAXIMUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long dress or skirt reaching the ankles, so it names a garment.

clue.text: Gelatin is in vitreous vessel

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a glass is a drinking vessel made of vitreous material

explanation.surface: Some jelly sitting in a glass container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it is simply two letters in the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a pure form of gelatin obtained from fish bladders, used to clarify beer and wine.

clue.text: Remain holding British pounds securely

indicators.note: a word holding others has them inside it, wrapping around them

blocks.note: to stay is to remain
B is the abbreviation for British
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Keep your sterling safely stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' suggests hitting or money in general, but it is just the sterling symbol L.
explanation.definitionFit: Stably means in a firm, steady way that will not shift, much like securely.

clue.text: Stagger, nearly attacked by a wasp

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a wasp attack leaves you stung

explanation.surface: Someone reeling after almost being stung by a wasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reeling about, but it means astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish them deeply, which is what stun means figuratively.

clue.text: Working at basic lab, getting paid leave

indicators.note: working letters are being moved about and put to use in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist toiling in an elementary laboratory and still earning holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabbatical is a period of paid time away from duties, granted especially to academics for study or travel.

clue.text: Problem about large area of poor housing

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big problem concerning a run-down housing district.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is an overcrowded, squalid urban district where the poorest people live.

clue.text: Greedily wanting one new standard assessment task, one in competent style

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for new
SAT stands for standard assessment task, a UK school test
the Roman numeral for one again
to do something ably is to do it competently

explanation.surface: An exam candidate hungry for results who sits a school test with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in' looks like a container instruction, but the 'in' belongs to the last phrase: in competent style is ABLY. SATs are national tests taken in English primary schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiably describes wanting more without ever being satisfied, which is how greed behaves.

clue.text: A US city — whichever one

blocks.note: taken as written
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Picking an American city at random.
explanation.definitionFit: Any, as in 'take any card', means one chosen without restriction.

clue.text: Historian girl is entertained by lieutenant

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a girl's name
taken as written
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A young woman being wined and dined by an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' sounds social, but it means held inside the abbreviation for lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year records of events, so is a kind of historian or chronicler.

clue.text: Plant unknown in Northern Ireland area

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
taken as written
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A mystery plant growing somewhere in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' invites putting the unknown inside NI, but it is just its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinnia is a garden flower of the daisy family with bright, many-petalled blooms.

clue.text: Robber's drunken manner with crew

blocks.note: high can mean intoxicated
a way of doing things is a manner
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A thief behaving like a drunk among his gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A highwayman was a mounted robber who held up travellers on the roads.

clue.text: What's regularly encountered in adults is some tendency to detachment

indicators.note: regularly met means picked up at even intervals, every other letter of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters

explanation.surface: A remark about how often grown-ups show a withdrawn streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Autism is a developmental condition often marked by difficulty with social interaction, which the setter loosely calls detachment.

clue.text: Cake is warmer at home

blocks.note: a muff is a fur tube that keeps the hands warm
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: The cake is hotter when eaten in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmer' looks like an adjective about the cake, but it is a noun: a thing that warms you.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small baked cake, either the sweet cupcake kind or the flat yeast bun.

clue.text: Sadly a girl is taken short

indicators.note: something taken short is cut off before its end, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman unfortunately caught needing the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken short' is a British idiom for suddenly needing the lavatory; here it just trims the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of grief, standing for 'sadly' or 'unfortunately' at the head of a sentence.

clue.text: Expect a delay

blocks.note: taken as written
a wait is a delay

explanation.surface: A weary traveller resigned to hold-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to look out for or anticipate it, so it means expect.

clue.text: Cheating with a huff until put right

indicators.note: putting something right means sorting and rearranging it into proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A partner sulking over an affair until things are patched up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheating partner is unfaithful, breaking a promise of fidelity.

clue.text: Keen to get a six on top of die

indicators.note: in a down entry one part placed on another sits above it
the top of a word in a column is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for six
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gambler eager to roll a six.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, a direct synonym of keen.

clue.text: One is a leader of Muslims

definitions.text: One is a leader of Muslims

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, the one at the front

blocks.note: 'one is' said by the speaker becomes 'I am', contracted to I'm
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A simple statement that a figure exists who guides the faithful of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and can be a Muslim community or religious leader.

clue.text: His maps I'd put in a mess somewhere on board

indicators.note: things put in a mess are scattered out of order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor's charts lie scattered somewhere aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' fits the naval surface, a ship's mess being where crew eat, but here it means disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle part of a ship, so it is a location on board.

clue.text: Dress used by ballerina twice the same day

blocks.note: Tu is the abbreviation for Tuesday, taken two times

explanation.surface: A dancer wearing the same costume on two occasions in one day.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt of layered net worn by ballet dancers.
